## Shadow AI visibility — demo mode

**This is a self-contained demo running on seeded data, not a live environment.** One Loki instance, ~11 example findings across every surface and OS, corporate domains fixed to `example.com` / `example.co.uk`. A few things differ from a real deployment:

- **Some panels are omitted.** The session gauges, registry-tools count, and last-scan-age tiles read Prometheus metrics; this demo runs Loki only, so those panels aren't included here. The full dashboard in `dashboards/` has them.
- **The corporate-domain variable is inert in the demo.** Work-vs-personal classification is hardcoded to the two example domains above, so editing the `Corporate domains` box won't change anything here. In a real deployment that regex drives the classification.
- **Time-based panels follow the time picker.** The findings are seeded once at startup; if the severity or surface charts look empty, widen the range (e.g. last 24h).

**Reading the board:** presence of a tool is informational. Red means a *personal* (non-corporate) account is signed into an AI tool on a managed device, or an unexplained integration was found — in a real deployment those route to your alerting channel automatically.

panels.description: Distinct devices that sent at least one finding in the last 24 hours, across all detection surfaces. Macs report through the day; Windows and network devices appear via the daily 06:00 scan. This is the total the two OS panels to the right break down.

targets.expr: count(count by (device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" [24h])))

panels.title: Devices reporting (24h)

panels.description: Devices from the 24h total whose findings include device-level macOS evidence (MDM inventory or the endpoint collector).

targets.expr: count(count by (device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" | os=`macos` [24h])))

panels.title: ...confirmed macOS

panels.description: Devices from the 24h total whose findings include device-level Linux evidence (RMM inventory).

targets.expr: count(count by (device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" | os=`linux` [24h])))

panels.title: ...confirmed Linux

panels.description: Devices from the 24h total whose findings include device-level Windows evidence (Intune inventory).

targets.expr: count(count by (device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" | os=`windows` [24h])))

panels.title: ...confirmed Windows

panels.description: The ten most widespread AI tools, counted as the number of distinct devices each was seen on in the last 7 days. Full list in the inventory table below.

targets.expr: topk(10, count by (tool) (count by (tool, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" [7d]))))

panels.title: Top tools (devices, 7d)

panels.description: Every person/tool/device seen in the last 7 days. Pinned to 7 days: the dashboard time picker does not change it. Filter with the Tool and Account type controls at the top. account_type: personal = a non-corporate account is signed in (needs a conversation), work = a corporate account (fine), none = the tool is present but no account was readable (e.g. an installed IDE extension), which is not the same as 'no account'.

targets.expr: count by (user, tool, surface, account_type, account_domain, device, severity) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format device=`{{ if .device_name }}{{ .device_name }}{{ else }}{{ .device }}{{ end }}` | label_format account_type=`{{ if eq .account_domain "" }}none{{ else if or (eq .account_domain "example.com") (eq .account_domain "example.co.uk") }}work{{ else }}personal{{ end }}` | tool =~ `${tool:regex}` | account_type =~ `$account` [7d]))

panels.title: Who is running what (last 7 days, filterable)

panels.description: Where the evidence comes from: browser = login pages, cli/ide/mcp/desktop = on the device itself, network = DNS traffic, cloud = Microsoft 365 records.

targets.expr: sum by (surface) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} [$__auto]))

panels.title: Findings by surface (7d)

panels.description: Reporting activity over time. Green (info) = tools being present, normal. Yellow (warn) = personal accounts or unexplained integrations - each also goes to Slack. A flat-zero chart means reporting has stopped, which is itself a problem.

targets.expr: sum by (severity) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} [$__auto]))

panels.title: Findings by severity (rate)

panels.description: Distinct devices per detection surface and platform over 7 days. A device appears on every surface it was seen on, so the column does not sum to the device total.

targets.expr: count by (surface, os) (count by (surface, os, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" | label_format os=`{{ if eq .os "" }}pre-os{{ else if eq .os "unknown" }}n/a (cloud/network){{ else }}{{ .os }}{{ end }}` [7d])))

panels.title: Surface x OS (devices, 7d)

panels.description: All findings by device platform. 'n/a (cloud/network)' is evidence from sources that cannot know the platform (sign-in logs, DNS, email) - expected, not an error.

targets.expr: sum by (os) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | label_format os=`{{ if eq .os "" }}pre-os{{ else if eq .os "unknown" }}n/a (cloud/network){{ else }}{{ .os }}{{ end }}` [7d]))

panels.title: Findings by OS (7d)

panels.description: The raw record of recent warnings - personal accounts and unexplained integrations - newest first. Each of these also produced a Slack alert.

targets.expr: {app="ai-guard-receiver"} | json | kind=`finding` | severity=`warn`

panels.title: Recent warn findings

panels.description: The complete list of AI tools detected in the last 7 days and how many devices each appears on. This is the living replacement for the monthly manual audit.

targets.expr: count by (tool) (count by (tool, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | device != "" | tool !~ ".*-mcp:.*" | source != `sentinelone_bridge` [7d])))

panels.title: AI tool inventory (all tools, by device count, 7d)

panels.description: Distinct devices with any finding in 7 days, by platform. A device with both device-level and network evidence is counted under each - see the reconciling stats at the top for exclusive counts.

targets.expr: count by (os) (count by (device, os) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format os=`{{ if eq .os "" }}pre-os{{ else if eq .os "unknown" }}n/a (cloud/network){{ else }}{{ .os }}{{ end }}` | __error__=`` [7d])))

panels.title: Devices with findings, by OS

panels.description: Integrations people have connected to their AI tools (MCP servers): which integration, who, and on which device. Not alarming by default - this is an inventory for review.

targets.expr: count by (tool, user, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format device=`{{ if .device_name }}{{ .device_name }}{{ else }}{{ .device }}{{ end }}` | tool =~ ".*-mcp:.*" [7d]))

panels.title: MCP integrations (who wired what, 7d)

panels.description: Every Anthropic surface in one place. The tool column shows why one product appears under several names: claude.ai is the browser extension reporting a domain, claude-code is the CLI and the IDE extension, claude is the desktop app, and anthropic.claude-code is the raw VS Code extension ID from before tool-name normalisation (those age out of the 7 day window on their own). Approved tool, so work accounts here are expected; personal accounts are the ones to act on.

targets.expr: count by (tool, surface, user, account_type, account_domain, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format account_type=`{{ if eq .account_domain "" }}none{{ else if or (eq .account_domain "example.com") (eq .account_domain "example.co.uk") }}work{{ else }}personal{{ end }}` | tool =~ `claude.*|anthropic\.claude.*` [7d]))

panels.title: Claude (Anthropic, all surfaces)

panels.description: chatgpt.com is the browser extension reporting a domain; chatgpt is the desktop app or IDE extension. ChatGPT is marked approved: false in the registry by default, so presence alerts here are informational until an approval decision is made. Personal accounts are the real signal.

targets.expr: count by (tool, surface, user, account_type, account_domain, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format account_type=`{{ if eq .account_domain "" }}none{{ else if or (eq .account_domain "example.com") (eq .account_domain "example.co.uk") }}work{{ else }}personal{{ end }}` | tool =~ `chatgpt.*|openai\.chatgpt.*` [7d]))

panels.title: ChatGPT (OpenAI, all surfaces)

panels.description: Account identity comes from the id_token JWT inside ~/.codex/auth.json, so the account domain here is who the CLI is actually signed in as. The heaviest source of personal accounts on developer machines.

targets.expr: count by (tool, surface, user, account_type, account_domain, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format account_type=`{{ if eq .account_domain "" }}none{{ else if or (eq .account_domain "example.com") (eq .account_domain "example.co.uk") }}work{{ else }}personal{{ end }}` | tool =~ `codex.*` [7d]))

panels.title: Codex CLI (OpenAI)

panels.description: Meeting transcription, so the data path matters more than the tool: transcripts of internal calls leave the estate. Cloud surface findings have no device, because the evidence is an Entra sign-in or a mailbox rather than a machine. Relevant to the plan tier question: SSO, EU data residency and SCIM are Enterprise-only.

targets.expr: count by (tool, surface, user, account_type, account_domain, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format account_type=`{{ if eq .account_domain "" }}none{{ else if or (eq .account_domain "example.com") (eq .account_domain "example.co.uk") }}work{{ else }}personal{{ end }}` | tool =~ `fireflies.*` [7d]))

panels.title: Fireflies
Pastes stopped (7d)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `paste (?P<action>\w+): (?P<detectors>[^\"]*)` | action=~`warned|blocked` [7d])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Paste/drop events where the browser extension's paste guard intercepted a secret pattern.

panels.title: Overridden (7d)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `paste (?P<action>\w+): (?P<detectors>[^\"]*)` | action=`overridden` [7d])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Times a person clicked Paste anyway after a warning. This is the number that decides when warn becomes block.

panels.title: Paste guard: active devices (24h)

targets.expr: count(count by (device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `heartbeat version=(?P<version>\S+) mode=(?P<pastemode>\S+)` | version!="" [24h]))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Devices whose paste guard sent a heartbeat in the last 24h. A heartbeat proves the whole chain works on that device; compare against your MDM scope count.

targets.expr: sum by (tool) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `paste (?P<action>\w+): (?P<detectors>[^\"]*)` | action!="" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Paste-guard detail (7d)

targets.expr: count by (action, detectors, tool, device) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format device=`{{ if .device_name }}{{ .device_name }}{{ else }}{{ .device }}{{ end }}` | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `paste (?P<action>\w+): (?P<detectors>[^\"]*)` | action!="" [7d]))

panels.description: Multi-detector pastes appear as a comma-joined detectors value; that is the extension's report shape.

panels.title: Paste guard: device coverage (24h)

targets.expr: count by (device, version, pastemode) (count_over_time({app="ai-guard-receiver", kind="finding"} | json | label_format device=`{{ if .device_name }}{{ .device_name }}{{ else }}{{ .device }}{{ end }}` | source=`paste_guard` | regexp `heartbeat version=(?P<version>\S+) mode=(?P<pastemode>\S+)` | version!="" [24h]))

panels.description: Per-device paste guard state from heartbeats: which extension version is running and which mode it is in.

list.description: Regex of account domains that count as corporate/work. Escape dots. Everything else with a non-empty domain shows as personal.
list.label: Corporate domains (regex)
list.name: corp_domains
